# Disruptivity Should Make Sense [bold]Self-Antagonism is allowed within reason[/bold]. You are permitted to intentionally violate SOP and Corporate Law, disrupt work, and neglect your duties, provided you have a good IC justification.
You must have this justification well established before you can act in such ways. Simply disliking someone or their department is not enough.
## Acceptable Vs. Unacceptable You are allowed to enter feuds with other individuals or departments, escalate severe matters into physical violence, and take whatever means are required to fulfil your Moods or Laws if they are applicable to you.
[bold]You may not break the server rules, cause an evaucation-worthy crisis, or derail an ongoing event.[/bold] You should also not act with malice, regardless of how much you might dislike an individual or their department.
Security and Command personnel are held to [textlink="higher standards" link="ClauseSpL1"], and should avoid becoming part of the problems they have been explicitly assigned to prevent.
## Sympathies And Coercion You may sympathize with but not willingly and freely act as a second agent to an antagonist or other bad faith actor, although you are allowed to enter cooperation if you are coerced or threatened. You may act in minor capacities as an accomplice but should never be completing an antagonist's objective for them. You should not seek out antagonists with the intent of allowing yourself to become converted or coerced.
Security and Command personnel are held to [textlink="higher standards" link="ClauseSpL1"], and must prioritize their duties over friendships with individuals who violate SOP or break the law. They should also resist coercion and threats, but may relent if there is reasonable IC justification for doing so.
